title: Contractual latency-band architecture and phased deployment gates for inference models
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Define a clear, contract-grade SLO/SLA surface and a correlated set of phased deployment gates for hosting new model variants and major runtime changes. This ticket codifies latency bands, availability targets, error budgets, monitoring windows, and automated/manual gates that must pass before increasing traffic percentage during a rollout. The outcome will be a single reference artifact PM can use in PRDs and a checklist that the Console team can verify during canary and progressive releases.
scope_clarification: Include: hosted API model rollouts, Dedicated pool targeted updates, and Private control-plane flagging. Exclude: internal experimental A/B ramps not touching customer traffic, and upgrades limited to telemetry-only changes. This ticket does not change billing or pricing terms.
slo_spec: Availability: 99.95% monthly uptime measured per region (applies to hosted API endpoints and Dedicated tenant pools)
Latency bands (tail & median): small models (<= 4B): P50 <= 60ms, P95 <= 200ms; medium models (4B-13B): P50 <= 120ms, P95 <= 350ms; large models (>13B): P50 <= 220ms, P95 <= 600ms
Error budget: 0.05% monthly error budget (errors defined as HTTP 5xx or explicit model failure responses), with burn rate monitoring windows at 1h, 6h, and 72h
Operational thresholds: if 1h burn rate > 4x baseline or P95 latency regression > 30% relative to baseline, trigger rollback gate
Customer-facing SLA: For enterprise customers with dedicated contracts, availability guarantee mapped to 99.95% and credits defined in SLA document (refer to links)
rollout_gates: Gate 0 (Pre-flight): Automated smoke tests, baseline latency collected from synthetic traffic for 24h, infra capacity validated by ENG-4321
Gate 1 (Canary 0.5%): 60-minute monitoring window; criteria: no SLO breaches, error rate within expected variance, observability events triaged; if any severity-1 incidents, block progression
Gate 2 (Canary 5%): 6-hour window with continuous burn-rate checks; automated rollback if burn rate > 3x or P95 regression > 20% sustained > 30 minutes
Gate 3 (Ramp to 25%): 24-hour window; require manual PM + Eng sign-off if any regression trends seen; require cost-per-token telemetry to be within modeled forecast +/- 15%
Gate 4 (Full rollout): Final 72-hour stability window; must show sustained burn-rate <= 1.5x and no untriaged severity-1s in last 24h
acceptance_criteria: PM and Engineering have an agreed SLO table covering small/medium/large model classes and availability that can be included in PRDs
A Console checklist item exists to validate Gate 0-4 for any model rollout and is linked from the deployment flow
Automatic rollback rules implemented in runtime controller per Gate 1 and Gate 2 thresholds (ENG-4499 pulls these into runtime config)
On-call runbooks updated to include specific actions for SLO burn-rate and latency regressions
A synthetic dashboard is available showing the SLOs, current burn rates, and gate evaluation history for the last 30 days
decisions: Adopt discrete latency bands by model size rather than per-model SLOs for initial rollout to reduce cognitive overhead
Use rolling windows at 1h, 6h, 24h, and 72h for burn-rate detection to capture both flash and slow regressions
Rollback thresholds are automated for canaries up to 5% traffic; ramps above 5% require manual sign-off
SLA credit language will remain in legal artifacts; this ticket only defines operational targets and thresholds
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Telemetry noise causing false-positive rollbacks. Mitigation: require sustained thresholds across multiple windows and correlate with request sampling to confirm true regression
Risk: Phased gates slow down urgent fix rollouts. Mitigation: define an expedited emergency path that requires exec override + postmortem
Risk: Different perf for Private deployments due to customer infra. Mitigation: require baseline collection per-customer before applying the same gates
